title: Vibrating Conveyor
model_title: Vibrating (Oscillating) Conveyor — Leaf-Spring Rocker Type with Crank Drive

introduction.definition: A vibrating (oscillating) conveyor moves material along a trough by repeated small, angled strokes. The trough is supported on inclined leaf springs (rockers) and driven by an eccentric crank. Each stroke moves the trough forward and up, throwing the material slightly forward; on the return stroke the trough slides back underneath it. Many designs run near the natural frequency of the spring system, which keeps drive power low.
key_points: No belt or chain — trough is the only contact part
Gentle, easy-clean, good for hot/abrasive material
Spring angle sets the stroke direction

introduction.summary: A vibrating conveyor moves material along a trough by oscillating it on inclined springs or rockers. Each forward-upward stroke throws particles slightly ahead; they land further along before the trough returns. Used for hot, abrasive or delicate materials and for feeding, screening and cooling.

foundation: Anchor the base frame firmly — or use a balanced (counter-oscillating) design to reduce forces transmitted to the floor.
alignment: Survey the structure so all pulleys and idlers are square to the centre line; train the belt empty, then loaded.
piping: Chutes designed for the material trajectory to centre-load the belt; skirts and dust seals at loading points; belt cleaners and plough at the discharge.
commissioning: Check pull-wire emergency stops, belt-drift and speed switches; run empty and loaded; record take-up position and motor current.

routine.task: Check stroke, noise and material flow.

periodic.task: Inspect leaf springs and rubber bushes; check bolts.

overhaul.task: Replace springs, connecting-arm bushes and eccentric bearings.

lubrication: Eccentric shaft bearings: grease to schedule.

causes: Low stroke, worn bushes, sticky material
remedies: Adjust drive; replace bushes; clean trough

safety: Guard the drive; keep clear of the oscillating trough; lock out before clearing.

video_tutorials.title: Vibrating Conveyor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Vibrating Conveyor.
A vibrating (oscillating) conveyor moves material along a trough by repeated small, angled strokes.
The trough is supported on inclined leaf springs (rockers) and driven by an eccentric crank.
Each stroke moves the trough forward and up, throwing the material slightly forward; on the return stroke the trough slides back underneath it.
Typical applications include hot castings and foundry sand; food products (easy to clean, gentle); chemicals and abrasive granules; distribution and spreading.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Vibrating Conveyor works.
Material is fed onto the trough.
The eccentric drive turns and the connecting arm pushes the trough.
The inclined leaf springs guide the trough forward and up on each stroke.
Particles hop forward a little each cycle and discharge at the end.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Vibrating Conveyor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vibrating Conveyor.
Check stroke, noise and material flow.
Inspect leaf springs and rubber bushes; check bolts.
Replace springs, connecting-arm bushes and eccentric bearings.
Watch for leaf spring cracking: change in stroke, noise. Common cause: fatigue, over-stroke.
Watch for slow conveying: material piles up. Common cause: low stroke, worn bushes, sticky material.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
